raw.assessment: Preassembly plausibly provides an opportunity to detect incomplete kits and difficult fits, but its benefit is unmeasured. Current evidence does not establish the success targets: median time is 11 minutes, five customers reported component problems, and seven of ten unpackers succeeded unaided. Repeated three-compartment orders taking seven to nine minutes limit any account that assembly is uniformly too slow; mixed batches contain the long tail, but layout complexity and switching are confounded. Overlapping widths also limit a simple width-only explanation of insertion retries. No damage claims do not establish that preassembly prevented damage.

openings.claim: Some mixed-batch delay may arise from repeatedly identifying the required parts and checking different layouts; grouping equivalent orders could reduce this delay while retaining preassembly.
openings.delta: Distinguishes switching overhead from inherent layout complexity before changing the supplied product or shifting assembly to customers.
openings.prediction: For matched layouts and colors, grouped runs reduce selection/checking time relative to interleaved runs, with little change in insertion time or component accuracy.
openings.probe: Use reusable samples within the 15-sample allowance. Have both workers perform matched grouped and interleaved sequences, counterbalancing sequence order. Record selection, insertion, checking and packing separately; independently reconcile components to each order slip. Keep accepted-order production on schedule.
assumptions: A short bench trial fits available working time.
Grouping retains each accepted order identity, compartment count and color.
Sample reuse does not create unequal wear between conditions.

openings.claim: When the short partition is independently verified as correct, does an order-specific placement diagram improve unaided arrangement compared with the current three-layout diagram?
openings.delta: Separates placement ambiguity from missing or incorrect components instead of treating every customer difficulty as a packing error.
openings.prediction: If diagram ambiguity contributes, verified kits with an order-specific diagram produce fewer short-partition placement errors and requests for help.
openings.probe: Assign the ten participants to two comparable five-person groups using verified kits and the two diagram variants. Record correct unaided arrangement within ten minutes and short-partition errors. Treat results as exploratory. Before adoption, check replacement-diagram cost against both spending caps.
assumptions: Diagram production fits the fixed delivery date and cost limits.
Original parts, assortment capacity, footprint, exterior color and removable partitions are retained.
Prior familiarity is balanced; this small trial cannot establish the 90% population target.

raw.assessment: Timing and observed customer success miss targets; missing-part reports warrant verification. Mixed batches and short-partition confusion suggest opportunities without establishing causes. Require 59/60 complete orders, median time at most eight minutes, and 90% unaided arrangement success within every constraint. Neither hypothesis demonstrates these outcomes.

openings.claim: A reusable order-specific kitting board with one outlined position per required partition could expose omissions and layout-switch errors before insertion.
openings.delta: Turn the ordered arrangement into a physical empty-position checklist; transfer its complete kit together instead of repeatedly consulting shared shape bins.
openings.prediction: Matched mixed-layout sequences show fewer verified picking errors and less selection/checking time, with little insertion-time change. No improvement weakens the selection-switching explanation.
openings.probe: Make reusable spare-board outlines for accepted layouts with an exterior-color field. Both workers alternate methods on matched mixed sequences. Independently verify contents and separately time selection, insertion, checking and packing. Include preparation/reset labor; reject designs exceeding the shared budget or delivery date.
assumptions: Parts have distinguishable outlines or labels.
Boards fit the bench and can be prepared within remaining delivery time.

openings.claim: For layouts using a short partition, shipping it already seated in its ordered position could provide an assembly reference while the remaining partitions ship loose.
openings.delta: Retain one potentially informative assembly step; test whether its spatial cue removes ambiguity while saving other workshop insertion work.
openings.prediction: Customers place remaining parts unaided despite reduced workshop assembly; short-partition questions decrease. Dislodgement or increased confusion would undermine the benefit.
openings.probe: Compare incumbent and partial assemblies with ten participants, counterbalancing exposure across different layouts. Record first-exposure success separately, partition questions, dislodgement after ordinary packed handling, and total workshop time. Verify exact components, color, footprint and assortment capacity. Treat results as screening; proceed only within combined 500 initial and 0.40 recurring limits and the fixed date.
assumptions: The short partition stays seated without permanent bonding or extra structural parts.
Loose parts can be secured within the material allowance.

openings.claim: Grouping equivalent orders may reduce switching overhead.
openings.discriminator: Selection/checking improves; insertion and accuracy remain comparable.
openings.probe: Both workers counterbalance matched grouped/interleaved layouts and colors; independently verify contents and time four stages.
openings.uncertainty: Complexity confounds switching; reuse wear must balance.

openings.claim: Order-specific diagrams may resolve short-partition ambiguity.
openings.discriminator: Verified kits yield fewer placement errors/help requests.
openings.probe: Compare diagrams in two comparable five-person groups; record unaided arrangement within ten minutes.
openings.uncertainty: Balance familiarity; small trial cannot establish 90%.

openings.claim: Outlined kitting boards may expose omissions and switching errors.
openings.discriminator: Fewer verified picking errors; faster selection/checking, similar insertion.
openings.probe: Both workers alternate methods on matched mixed orders; independently verify components, time four stages including preparation/reset, and include color fields.
openings.uncertainty: Requires distinguishable parts, bench space and preparation time.

openings.claim: Preseating the short partition may cue arrangement while saving other insertion work.
openings.discriminator: Unaided success persists; questions fall despite partial assembly.
openings.probe: Counterbalance incumbent/partial layouts with ten participants; separate first exposure, check packed-handling dislodgement and total workshop time.
openings.uncertainty: Seating and loose-part security must work without permanent bonding or extra structural parts.

post_distill.decision: Screen within shared 15 samples, ten participants, 500 initial/0.40 recurring limits and fixed date. Preserve 30x20 footprint, assortment capacity, removable partitions, ordered counts/colors. Reconcile all contents; require 59/60 complete, median <=8 minutes, >=90% unaided. Causes remain unproven; widths alone and absent damage claims establish neither insertion cause nor preassembly protection.
